title: Squares of a Sorted Array
statement: Given a nondecreasing array `nums`, return an array of the squares of each value, also sorted nondecreasing.
hints: Squaring destroys sorted order when negatives are present, because a large negative becomes a large positive.
The largest square is at one of the two ends.
Fill the answer from the back, always taking the end whose absolute value is larger.

approaches.name: Two pointers
approaches.explanation: Merge the two increasing rays of absolute values.

editorial: On a sorted array the absolute values form a valley. Two pointers at the ends walk up both slopes, and the larger absolute value is written next into the result from right to left.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def sorted_squares(nums: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    left, right = 0, len(nums) - 1
    out = [0] * len(nums)
    for pos in range(len(nums) - 1, -1, -1):
        if abs(nums[left]) > abs(nums[right]):
            out[pos] = nums[left] * nums[left]
            left += 1
        else:
            out[pos] = nums[right] * nums[right]
            right -= 1
    return out
